title: A generic task model and control strategy to support learning, robust control, and generalization of contact-rich manipulation tasks
core_idea: Automatically derive an optimal reference frame for task models directly from recorded motion and wrench demonstrations using a hyperparameter-free probabilistic method grounded in screw theory; the frame maximizes decoupling between learned signals to enable design of a generic, decoupled, constraint-based velocity-resolved controller with few task-dependent parameters.
tldr: Provide an automatic, probabilistic, screw-theory-based method to find the best task reference frame from demonstration data so learned motion and force signals become decoupled and can be controlled by a simple generic decoupled controller.
